advisory.title: Lease test never shows an import holding the lease from fetch through cleanup; releasing it early would pass every test
advisory.fix: Hold the lease from a real import that pauses between fetch and cleanup, for example through a test-only hook or by blocking the final rebuild. While it is paused, run the second import from another process and assert Conflict and no ref change. That would fail if `let _lease = acquire_import_lease(...)` became `let _ = ...` or the guard were dropped before cleanup.

advisory.title: import_bundle_with_lease_timeout grew to 64 lines, over the 50-line function limit
advisory.evidence: fn import_bundle_with_lease_timeout(... ) spans lines 322-385 and now inlines: `let git_bundle_path = ...; if !git_bundle_path.is_file() {...}`, `let existing = namespace_refs(repo, &namespace)?; if let Some((branch, oid)) = existing.iter().find(|r| !heads.contains(r)) {...}`, `unbundle_git_objects(...)?; ensure_namespace_matches(...)?;`, `if !heads.iter().any(|(branch, _)| branch == "master") {...}`, and the cleanup loop.
advisory.fix: Keep behavior identical but extract the pre-merge leg (advertised_heads + pre-fetch namespace check + unbundle_git_objects + post-fetch ensure_namespace_matches + master check) into one helper, e.g. `fetch_payload_heads(repo, &git_bundle_path, &namespace, &payload_id) -> Result<Vec<(String,String)>>`, and the cleanup into `delete_payload_namespace(repo, &namespace, &payload_id, &heads)`. Lease acquisition stays in the caller so the guard's scope is unchanged.

advisory.title: payload_id is a noun-named I/O function, shadowed by a same-named local
advisory.evidence: fn payload_id(git_bundle_path: &Path) -> Result<String> { let mut file = std::fs::File::open(git_bundle_path)?; ... }  and later  `let payload_id = payload_id(&git_bundle_path)?;`
advisory.fix: Rename to `compute_payload_id` (verb-first, matching the existing `compute_bundle_checksum`) and update the call site and the test helper `payload_id_of`.

advisory.evidence:

fn parse_ref_lines(text: &str, what: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> { ... Ok((name.to_string(), oid.to_string())) }
advisory.fix: State the return order in the doc comment, e.g. "returns `(refname, oid)` pairs", so readers of the `(String, String)` tuples in advertised_heads/namespace_refs do not have to read the body.

advisory.evidence: /// master, resolving conflicts via the same libgit2 + CRDT pipeline the network-sync path uses (`SyncManager::apply_merge_result`).
advisory.fix: Rewrap to the surrounding ~90-column doc width; rustfmt does not wrap comments.

advisory.title: Lease test cannot tell whether the lease is held past fetch; a `let _ =` or early-drop regression passes every test
advisory.evidence: Test side: `let held = write_lock::acquire(&git_dir, "ddb-bundle-import.lock", Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap(); ... spawn_lease_child("refuse", dir2.path(), &bundle);`. Code side: `let _lease = acquire_import_lease(repo, lease_timeout)?;`. The only other lease checks are after the import returns: `write_lock::acquire(... Duration::from_millis(200)).expect("a failed import must release the import lease")`.
advisory.fix: Add a test that fails if the lease is dropped too early. Let an import hold the lease through merge, rebuild and cleanup, for example by blocking at a test-only hook after the merge or on a held rebuild or index resource. While it is blocked, have a second process or handle try `write_lock::acquire` on ddb-bundle-import.lock with a short timeout and assert that it times out. Alternatively assert the lease is still held at the post-merge failure point in bundle_import_keeps_refs_when_post_merge_work_fails. Probe to show the gap: change mod.rs:350 to `let _ = acquire_import_lease(repo, lease_timeout)?;`, then run `mise exec -- cargo +1.89.0 test -p ddb-core --lib bundle`. All tests are expected to still pass.

advisory.title: Strict ref-record parsing (never skip malformed branch records) has no test
advisory.evidence: `fn parse_ref_lines(text: &str, what: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> { ... .ok_or_else(|| DoogatError::Sync(format!("malformed {what} record: {line:?}")))?;` and `if branch.is_empty() { return Err(DoogatError::Sync(format!("malformed bundle head: {name}"))); }`. tests.rs has no reference to parse_ref_lines, advertised_heads or the word malformed (rg returned only the unrelated namespace_refs test name).
advisory.fix: Add a colocated unit test for parse_ref_lines. It should reject a short or uppercase OID, a line with no space, an empty name, a name with whitespace, and a blank line in the middle, each with a Sync error naming the record. It should accept both 40-hex and 64-hex OIDs. Also assert that advertised_heads-style filtering rejects `refs/heads/` with an empty branch and ignores HEAD and tags. Without this, changing `.map(...).collect()` to `.filter_map(...)` would silently skip malformed records and still pass every test, even though the card says to never skip them silently.

advisory.title: Wrong-OID namespace case does not isolate the pre-fetch refusal: the non-forced fetch would reject it anyway
advisory.evidence: `repo2.repo.reference(&format!("{ns}master"), local_head, false, "seed wrong oid")` followed by `assert!(matches!(err, DoogatError::Sync(_)) && err.to_string().contains(&ns), ...)`. local_head and the bundle's master are unrelated histories, so the non-forced `refs/heads/*:{namespace}*` fetch fails as non-fast-forward. run_git's `git {args} failed` message then also contains the namespace, so removing the `existing.iter().find(|r| !heads.contains(r))` pre-check still passes this case.
advisory.fix: Seed the wrong-OID ref with an ancestor of the bundle's master (a fetch would fast-forward it), or assert the refusal text `nothing was fetched, merged or deleted`, so the pre-fetch check is the only thing that can pass the case. Also assert that no objects were unbundled, for example that the bundle master OID is absent from repo2's odb.

advisory.title: Masterless-import error is not checked for the payload id and delivered branch names
advisory.evidence: The test asserts only `err.to_string().contains("bundle merge failed:")`, while the code emits `"bundle merge failed: bundle payload {payload_id} delivered no master branch (delivered: {delivered:?}); fetched refs kept under {namespace}"`. The card requires the error to carry the payload id and the delivered branch names.
advisory.fix: In failed_bundle_then_masterless_bundle_never_merges_stale_master, also assert that the error contains payload_id_of(&masterless) and "sidecar".

findings.title: Docs and comment call the namespace fetch "non-forced"; git forces updates under refs/remotes/ regardless, the pre-fetch check is the real guard
findings.evidence: bundle.md:58 says the fetch of refs/heads/* into refs/remotes/bundle/<payload-id>/* is "(non-forced)" and bundle/mod.rs:212-213 documents unbundle_git_objects as "(non-forced, never pruning)". git-fetch(1), refspec section: "any updates outside of refs/{tags,heads}/* will be accepted without + in the refspec (or --force)". So omitting `+` in `refs/heads/*:{namespace}*` (mod.rs:221) does not stop a non-fast-forward overwrite of an existing namespace ref; what stops it is the pre-fetch `namespace_refs` vs `advertised_heads` refusal at mod.rs:353-359. Correctness holds, but the doc names the wrong mechanism and a future reader could drop the pre-check believing fetch would refuse.
findings.fix: Reword bundle.md step 7 and the unbundle_git_objects doc comment: state that no `+`/`--force` is passed but git accepts non-fast-forward updates under refs/remotes/ anyway, which is why every preexisting namespace ref is checked against the advertised heads before the fetch runs.

findings.title: Post-merge failures (node registration, final index rebuild) escape raw without naming the kept namespace
findings.evidence: Merge failures append "(fetched refs kept under refs/remotes/bundle/<id>/)" (mod.rs:244-249), the masterless and refusal errors name the namespace (mod.rs:355-358, 366-369), but `import_node_registrations(repo, &work_dir)?` (373) and `index.rebuild(repo)?` (374) return the raw Io/Sqlite error with no pointer to the retained refs. The card's Docs section requires "Errors name the namespace; failed refs remain until a safe retry or operator recovery". The new test bundle_import_keeps_refs_when_post_merge_work_fails asserts only `result.is_err()`, so the message content is unpinned.
findings.fix: Before propagating an error from import_node_registrations or index.rebuild, emit `tracing::warn!(namespace = %namespace, "bundle import failed after merge; fetched refs kept")` or map the error to add "(fetched refs kept under {namespace})" while preserving its variant where the variant carries a String; extend the late-rebuild test to assert the namespace appears in the error or log.

findings.title: Unreachable match arm in merge_failed closure
findings.evidence: `merge_failed` does `match bundle_merge_error(e) { DoogatError::Sync(msg) => ..., other => other }` but `bundle_merge_error` (mod.rs:279-281) unconditionally returns `DoogatError::Sync(...)`, so the `other => other` arm is dead code introduced by this change.
findings.fix: Collapse to `let merge_failed = |e| DoogatError::Sync(format!("bundle merge failed: {e} (fetched refs kept under refs/remotes/bundle/{payload_id}/)"))`, or have bundle_merge_error return the formatted String and wrap once.
